title_tag: 大国掰手腕，小国发大财：谁在中美竞争中坐收渔利？—— 英国《经济学人》外刊讲解第1216天
h1: 大国掰手腕，小国发大财：谁在中美竞争中坐收渔利？
category: 英国《经济学人》外刊讲解 第1216天
nav_hint: Critical minerals and the US-China rivalry

headline.en_html: The countries making a fortune from the US-China rivalry Critical-mineral profits could transform a lucky few
headline.zh: 大国掰手腕，小国发横财——谁在中美对抗中坐收渔利？关键矿产的暴利，或许能彻底改写少数几个幸运儿的命运——但这份"幸运"，只属于寥寥数人。

notes.en: make a fortune means to earn or obtain a very large amount of money
notes.zh: "造出一大笔钱"（fortune 来自罗马神话命运女神Fortuna，本义"命运、运气"——古人认为有钱没钱靠命，钱是命运塞给你的），财富语境核心义为发大财、赚大钱
notes.ctx: 作者不用earn（一分耕耘一分收获地挣）、不用get rich（变富），而用make a fortune——这钱是"风口上躺着发出来的"，带运气味。且用进行时 making，现在分词作后置定语修饰the countries，强调"正在发生"。标题埋了钩子：主角是中美对抗，发财的却是第三方国家
notes.ex1: She made a fortune buying apartments before the boom.她在房价暴涨前买房发了大财。
notes.ex2: This ring cost me a fortune, but she loves it.这戒指花了我一大笔钱，但她很喜欢。

notes.en: rivalry means a situation in which people, companies or countries compete with each other for the same thing
notes.zh: "共河而争"（rival 来自拉丁语 rivalis——rivus 是"河"，rivalis 是"同住一条河边、共用一条河的人"），竞争语境核心义为对抗、较劲、你死我活的竞争
notes.ex1: Sibling rivalry is common in families with two children close in age.年龄相近的两个孩子之间，兄弟姐妹的争宠较劲很常见。
notes.ex2: The rivalry between the two tech giants has lasted a decade.这两家科技巨头之间的对抗已经持续了十年。

notes.en: a critical mineral is a mineral considered essential for a country's economy, technology or national security, whose supply is at risk
notes.zh: "没它不行的矿"，政策与产业语境核心义为关键矿产、战略矿产
notes.ctx: 一句话记死——AI 靠芯片，芯片要镓、锗、铟；电动车靠电池，电池要锂、钴、铜；导弹战斗机要稀土、要钨。缺一样，手机、汽车、军队全停摆。这是全文的"命脉"概念，理解它，后面所有矿名才不是空的
notes.ex1: Governments are racing to secure critical mineral supplies for their industries.各国政府正竞相为本国产业锁定关键矿产供应。
notes.ex2: The new law is designed to protect domestic critical mineral resources.这项新法旨在保护本国的关键矿产资源。

notes.en: a lucky few means a small number of people or places who are fortunate
notes.zh: "少数几个幸运儿"（lucky 幸运+ few 少数），描述语境核心义为寥寥几个幸运儿
notes.ctx: few 的坑——few 单独用是"几乎没有"（否定），a few 是"几个"（肯定），the few 是"少数派"。作者用a lucky few 而非some/many，一落笔就埋好结论：能从这波矿产潮发财的，不是所有资源国，只有寥寥几个。lucky 尤其损——它们发财靠命好、脚下正好有矿，不靠本事
notes.ex1: Only a lucky few got tickets to the final. 只有少数几个幸运儿买到了决赛门票。
notes.ex2: Few countries have both the deposits and the ability to process them. 几乎没有哪个国家既有矿藏、又有加工能力。

paragraphs.en_html: <mark class="voc">For better or worse</mark>, many poor countries’ fortunes <mark class="voc">hinge on</mark> their natural resources. Since their industries are less <mark class="voc">sophisticated</mark> and their service sectors smaller than in rich places, an underground <mark class="voc">bounty</mark> can <mark class="voc">make a big difference to</mark> their economic prospects. Rising global demand for oil or ores can <mark class="voc">spur</mark> growth, attract investment and fill fiscal holes.
paragraphs.zh: 无论好坏，许多穷国的命运都系于脚下的资源——它们的工业不如富国精密，服务业规模也更小，地底下的慷慨馈赠，便成了改写经济前景的那张牌。全球对石油与矿石的需求不断攀升，恰似一记马刺，催动增长、引来投资，也补上了政府的财政窟窿。

notes.en: for better or worse means whatever the outcome is, whether it is good or bad
notes.zh: "无论好坏"（出自西方婚礼誓词for better, for worse, for richer, for poorer），承诺与宿命语境核心义为无论如何、不管好坏
notes.ctx: 作者用婚礼誓词开头，暗示穷国与地底资源像一对"被命运绑死的夫妻"——这婚离不掉，好坏都捆在一起。也埋伏笔：资源可能是祝福，也可能是诅咒
notes.ex1: For better or worse, the two families are now tied together.无论如何，这两个家族如今已经绑在了一起。
notes.ex2: She stayed with him, for better or worse, for thirty years.无论好坏，她跟他一起过了三十年。

notes.en: hinge on means to depend completely on one thing
notes.zh: "铰在……上"（hinge 门上的合页——门整个吊在合页上，门会不会掉全看它），取决语境核心义为完全取决于、悬于一点
notes.ctx: 比depend on 狠——depend on 是"依赖"，中性；hinge on 是"整件事悬在这一个点上，这点崩了全完蛋"。穷国的命像一扇门吊在合页上，那个合页就是地底下的矿
notes.ex1: The whole deal hinges on whether the bank approves the loan.整笔交易就取决于银行是否批准这笔贷款。
notes.ex2: Her future hinges on the result of this one exam.她的未来就悬在这一场考试的结果上。

notes.en: sophisticated means highly developed and complex; it can also describe a person who is worldly and knowledgeable
notes.zh: "有智慧的"（词根soph- 来自希腊语sophia"智慧"；古希腊智者叫sophist），工业语境核心义为复杂精密的、先进的；另一义为世故老练的
notes.ctx: industries are less sophisticated 取"精密、高级"义。与advanced （先进）、developed（发达）不同，sophisticated 强调"内里复杂、有技术含量"。说一个工业less sophisticated，不是说它没工业，是它干的是低端初级活
notes.ex1: The new factory uses highly sophisticated machinery.新工厂使用高度精密的机器。
notes.ex2: Poorer countries often have less sophisticated industries than rich ones.穷国的工业通常不如富国精密高级。

notes.en: bounty means a generous gift, or money given as a reward
notes.zh: "好处、赠予"（词根bon- 来自拉丁语bonus"好"；同源bonus 奖金、bon voyage 一路顺风），财富语境核心义为慷慨的赠予、丰厚的赏金
notes.ex1: The region enjoys a bounty of natural resources.这个地区享有丰富的自然资源。
notes.ex2: A bounty hunter tracked down the escaped criminal for the reward.一名赏金猎人为拿赏金追捕到了那名逃犯。

notes.en: make a big difference to means to have a large and important effect on someone or something
notes.zh: "制造出巨大的不同"，影响语境核心义为对……产生巨大影响
notes.ctx: 高频短语make a difference（产生影响）的加强版。注意介词是to—— make a difference TO something。有没有这笔矿，对穷国是天差地别
notes.ex1: A little extra sleep can make a big difference to your mood. 多睡一小会儿能对你的情绪产生很大影响。
notes.ex2: Foreign investment makes a big difference to a small economy. 外资对小体量经济能产生巨大影响。

notes.en: spur means to encourage something to happen or develop faster
notes.zh: "用马刺踢一脚"（spur 牛仔靴后跟带尖刺的金属片，往马肚子一夹马就往前冲），刺激语境核心义为刺激、促进、推动
notes.ctx: 比encourage（拍肩膀"加油"）狠——是拿马刺"踢你一脚"。全球需求一涨，像往穷国经济屁股上踢了一马刺。另记高频习语on the spur of the moment（一时冲动）
notes.ex1: Rising demand for copper has spurred investment in new mines. 铜需求的上升刺激了对新矿的投资。
notes.ex2: On the spur of the moment, I booked a flight to the coast. 一时冲动，我订了张飞往海边的机票。

paragraphs.en_html: Now the world may be entering another <mark class="voc">supercycle</mark>, <mark class="voc">propelled</mark> by the race between America and China to secure supplies of minerals critical to artificial intelligence, <mark class="voc">electrification</mark> and other technologies expected to define the 21st century. Chinese <mark class="voc">minerals diplomacy</mark> is <mark class="voc">alive and well</mark>. Donald Trump’s administration has already signed <mark class="voc">mineral-themed</mark> agreements with more than 20. Today the rivals are both <mark class="voc">courting</mark> a much smaller group of countries <mark class="voc">capable of</mark> getting minerals out of the ground quickly.
paragraphs.zh: 如今，世界或许正迈入又一轮超级周期，推手正是中美两国那场争夺关键矿产供应的竞赛——这些矿产，关乎人工智能、电气化，以及那些注定要定义21世纪的技术。中国的矿产外交方兴未艾，川总政府也已与二十余国签下矿产协议。然而时至今日，两个对手真正放下身段去讨好的，是寥寥无几、能把矿产快速挖出地面的国家。

notes.en: supercycle means an unusually long period of strong growth and high prices for commodities
notes.zh: "超级周期"（super- 超级+ cycle 周期），经济语境核心义为大宗商品价格的超长上涨期
notes.ctx: 矿、油、铜这些原材料价格不是年年平稳，而是"憋很多年猛涨一大波"。上一轮是2000 年代中国崛起推动——铁矿石从13 涨到190 美元/吨（13 倍）、铜 1800 到8900（近4 倍）、石油25 到147（近6 倍）。每一轮超级周期背后都站着一个"巨人在崛起"
notes.ex1: Many analysts believe we are entering a new commodity supercycle. 许多分析师认为我们正进入一个新的大宗商品超级周期。
notes.ex2: The last supercycle was driven by China's rapid urbanisation. 上一轮超级周期是由中国快速城市化推动的。

notes.en: propel means to push or drive something forward
notes.zh: "往前推"（pro- 向前+ pel 推；同源propeller 螺旋桨），推动语境核心义为推动、推进
notes.ex1: The boom was propelled by a race between the two superpowers. 这波繁荣是由两个超级大国之间的竞赛推动的。
notes.ex2: Her first film propelled her to international fame. 她的第一部电影把她推向了国际声誉。

notes.en: electrification means the process of changing something so that it uses electricity instead of other forms of power
notes.zh: "电气化"（electr- 电+ -ification ……化），产业语境核心义为电气化、把烧油烧煤的东西换成用电
notes.ex1: The electrification of transport is driving demand for lithium and copper. 交通电气化正推高对锂和铜的需求。
notes.ex2: Rural electrification brought power to millions of homes. 农村电气化为数百万家庭带来了电力。

notes.en: minerals diplomacy means the use of diplomatic and financial tools by a government to secure access to minerals abroad
notes.zh: "矿产外交"（minerals 矿产+ diplomacy 外交），国际事务语境核心义为矿产外交、用外交手段去搞矿
notes.ctx: 就是政府出面，去资源国投资、签协议、拿矿权。Chinese minerals diplomacy is alive and well 是客观陈述——在矿产外交上中国一直走得很早、很活跃
notes.ex1: Minerals diplomacy has become central to both powers' foreign policy. 矿产外交已成为两个大国对外政策的核心。
notes.ex2: The country uses resource diplomacy to win allies in the region. 该国利用资源外交在地区内争取盟友。

notes.en: alive and well means still active and successful, and not in decline
notes.zh: "活着且健康"，状态语境核心义为依然活跃、一点没衰败
notes.ctx: 固定短语。形容某个做法、机构、关系"还活得好好的"。Chinese minerals diplomacy is alive and well——中国的矿产外交依然活跃、势头不减
notes.ex1: Despite the rumours, the old tradition is alive and well. 尽管有流言，这项老传统依然活跃。
notes.ex2: The industry, once thought doomed, is alive and well. 这个一度被认为没救的行业依然生机勃勃。

notes.en: -themed is used after a noun to form an adjective meaning "having a particular theme or subject"
notes.zh: "以……为主题的"（theme 主题+ -d），构词语境核心义为……主题的
notes.ctx: mineral-themed agreements 矿产主题的协议。这个后缀极能产—— music-themed 音乐主题、Christmas-themed 圣诞主题、horror-themed 恐怖主题
notes.ex1: The two sides signed a series of mineral-themed agreements. 双方签署了一系列矿产主题的协议。
notes.ex2: The hotel threw a Christmas-themed party for guests. 这家酒店为客人办了一场圣诞主题的派对。

notes.en: court (as a verb) means to try to please someone or get their support, often in a way that seems flattering
notes.zh: "求爱、献殷勤"（court 本义庭院、法庭，动词化"追、讨好"），拉拢语境核心义为献殷勤、讨好、争取
notes.ctx: 最原始画面是小伙子追姑娘、送花献殷勤。引申为"放下身段去讨好争取"。中美两个大国为矿，像追对象一样去哄一群小国——平时穷国求大国，现在大国求穷国，本身是反转。另记court disaster（自找麻烦）
notes.ex1: Both superpowers are courting the same small group of countries. 两个超级大国都在讨好同样那一小群国家。
notes.ex2: By ignoring the warning, he was courting disaster. 无视警告，他是在自找麻烦。

notes.en: capable of means having the ability or qualities necessary to do something
notes.zh: "装得下、办得到的"（capable 有能力的+ of），能力语境核心义为有能力做……
notes.ex1: Only a few countries are capable of producing these minerals quickly. 只有少数几个国家能快速生产这些矿物。
notes.ex2: She is more than capable of running the whole operation. 她完全有能力运营整个业务。

paragraphs.en_html: On October 16th the World Bank said it would <mark class="voc">quintuple</mark>, to $20bn, a fund to help countries <mark class="voc">capture</mark> some of the surging demand. Yet in order to succeed, their governments cannot rely only on their <mark class="voc">subterranean</mark> resources or their <mark class="voc">cosiness</mark> with America and China. They must also show ability to supply stuff <mark class="voc">at speed</mark>. The urgency is <mark class="voc">palpable</mark>. In May 2025 Mr Trump was forced to <mark class="voc">rein in</mark> tariffs he had <mark class="voc">imposed on</mark> Chinese goods, after China <mark class="voc">retaliated</mark> by restricting exports of seven rare-earth minerals used to make semiconductors and weapons. America wants to break China’s <mark class="voc">chokehold</mark>.
paragraphs.zh: 10月16日，世界银行宣布将一支基金扩至五倍、达200亿美元，以助各国分食这波暴涨的需求。然而，要真正成功，这些国家的政府不能只仰仗地下的资源，也不能只凭与中美两国的亲密关系——它们还得拿出高速供货的本事。局势之紧迫，触手可及。2025年5月，川总被迫收回先前加诸中国商品的关税，起因是中国出手反制，限制七种用于制造半导体与武器的稀土出口。如今，美国一心想要挣脱中国锁在喉咙上的那只手。

notes.en: quintuple means to become five times as large, or to multiply by five
notes.zh: "翻五倍"（词根quint- 拉丁语"五"；同源quintet 五重奏），数字语境核心义为增至五倍
notes.ctx: 倍数全家桶一次记——single 一倍、double 两倍、triple 三倍、 quadruple 四倍、quintuple 五倍。世行把基金扩大到五倍、至200 亿美元，而五年前这类融资才约36 亿，翻五倍还多
notes.ex1: The fund will quintuple to twenty billion dollars. 这支基金将扩大五倍，达到两百亿美元。
notes.ex2: Profits tripled last year after the new mine opened. 新矿投产后，利润去年翻了三倍。

notes.en: capture, in this sense, means to get control of a share of something such as a market or demand
notes.zh: "捕获、俘虏"（capture a criminal 抓罪犯），商务语境引申义为抢占、分得
notes.ctx: capture some of the surging demand——从暴涨的需求里抢下一块、分一杯羹。capture the market 抢占市场、capture a share 分得份额，都是外刊高频
notes.ex1: The fund aims to help poor countries capture a share of the demand. 这支基金旨在帮助穷国分得需求的一杯羹。
notes.ex2: The new brand quickly captured a large share of the market. 这个新品牌迅速抢占了很大的市场份额。

notes.en: subterranean means existing or happening under the ground
notes.zh: "地底下的"（sub- 下面+ terr- 土地+ -anean 形容词后缀；同根terrain 地形、 territory 领土、terrestrial 陆地的），书面语境核心义为地下的
notes.ctx: 作者不用口语词underground，偏用地质学书面词subterranean，是外刊的"端着"。知道它俩一个意思即可。subterranean resources = 地底下的矿
notes.ex1: The country cannot rely only on its subterranean resources.这个国家不能只靠它地底下的资源。
notes.ex2: A subterranean river runs beneath the city.一条地下河在城市下方流淌。

notes.en: cosiness (also cosiness) means a close and comfortable relationship; friendliness
notes.zh: "舒适、惬意"（cozy 舒适的），关系语境引申义为亲密关系、走得近
notes.ctx: 熟词僻义的坑——你学cozy 是a cozy room（舒适的房间），但 cosiness with America and China 不是"舒服"，是"亲密、套近乎"。get cozy with somebody 即"跟某人打得火热"。这里指资源国抱大国的大腿
notes.ex1: Their cosiness with the big powers has brought them money. 它们与大国的亲密关系给它们带来了钱。
notes.ex2: He got a little too cozy with the company he was supposed to regulate. 他与他本该监管的那家公司走得太近了。

notes.en: at speed means quickly or at a high rate
notes.zh: "以高速"，能力语境核心义为快速地、高速地
notes.ctx: supply stuff at speed 快速供货。与P2 的"能快速把矿挖出来"扣在一起——作者在一个"快"字上反复敲，胜负手就一个字：快。光有矿、光抱大腿都不够，还得供得快
notes.ex1: The winners are those who can supply minerals at speed. 赢家是那些能快速供应矿产的国家。
notes.ex2: The project must be delivered at speed to meet demand. 这个项目必须快速交付以满足需求。

notes.en: palpable means so obvious or strong that it can almost be felt
notes.zh: "摸得着的"（词根palp- 摸；同源palpate 触诊——医生按肚子检查），程度语境核心义为真切可感的、明显到能摸到的
notes.ctx: 比obvious（眼睛看出的"明显"）更强——palpable 是"用手实实在在摸到的"。作者不说"紧迫感很明显"，说"紧迫感摸得着"，把局势之紧写到极致。The urgency is palpable
notes.ex1: The tension in the room was palpable before the announcement. 宣布之前，房间里的紧张感扑面而来。
notes.ex2: There was a palpable sense of excitement among the crowd. 人群中涌动着真切可感的兴奋。

notes.en: rein in means to control or limit something that is getting out of hand
notes.zh: "勒住缰绳"（rein 缰绳——马跑太快，骑手一勒缰绳马就慢下来），控制语境核心义为收紧、控制、收回
notes.ctx: 比control 多一层狼狈——"本来已经放出去，现在不得不硬拽回来"。川总之前猛加关税，加猛了，被逼着一根一根往回勒。rein in tariffs 收回关税
notes.ex1: The government was forced to rein in the tariffs it had imposed. 政府被迫收回了之前加征的关税。
notes.ex2: The board moved to rein in runaway costs. 董事会着手控制失控的成本。

notes.en: impose on means to officially force something such as a tax, rule or punishment on someone
notes.zh: "把……强加于"（im- 上+ pose 放→ 放到人头上），施政语境核心义为征收、强加、施加
notes.ctx: impose tariffs 征税、impose sanctions 施加制裁。he had imposed on Chinese goods 用过去完成时，强调"先前已经加上的、现在要收回的"
notes.ex1: The president imposed tariffs on a wide range of Chinese goods. 总统对中国多种商品加征了关税。
notes.ex2: The court imposed a heavy fine on the company.法院对该公司处以重罚。

notes.en: retaliate means to do something bad to someone because they have done something bad to you
notes.zh: "以牙还牙"（re- 回+ 拉丁语talio"同态复仇"——你打我一下我也打你一下），冲突语境核心义为反击、报复
notes.ctx: 比revenge（个人恩怨、带情绪）更冷静对等，国家之间常用。中国 retaliated by restricting exports——你卡我的货，我也卡你的，限制七种稀土出口
notes.ex1: China retaliated by restricting exports of seven rare-earth minerals.中国以限制七种稀土矿物出口作为反击。
notes.ex2: The country threatened to retaliate against any new tariffs.该国威胁要对任何新关税进行报复。

notes.en: chokehold means a strong control over something that makes it very difficult for others to act freely
notes.zh: "锁喉"（choke 窒息+ hold 控制——格斗里从背后勒住脖子），控制语境核心义为钳制、卡脖子
notes.ctx: 比monopoly（垄断）更狠——画面是一只手指在喉咙上喘不上气。 America wants to break China's chokehold，用美国视角：中国控制稀土加工，像一只手锁住它的喉咙。全文关键词之一
notes.ex1: America wants to break China's chokehold on rare-earth processing.美国想打破中国对稀土加工的控制。
notes.ex2: The company had a chokehold on the supply of the key material.这家公司牢牢卡住了这种关键材料的供应。

paragraphs.en_html: The <mark class="voc">wheedling</mark> has worked. According to officials, in 2025 the American government and American firms spent $15.4bn on foreign mines, up from nearly nothing in 2024, and more is expected this year. <mark class="voc">In response</mark>, Chinese state-owned mining giants <mark class="voc">splurged</mark> well over $30bn abroad, far more than in 2024.
paragraphs.zh: 这番软磨硬泡，到底起了效。据官员透露，2025年美国政府与企业向海外矿山砸下154亿美元，而2024年这个数字几乎为零，今年料将更多。作为回应，中国的国有矿业巨头在海外豪掷远超300亿美元，远胜往年。

notes.en: wheedle means to persuade someone to do something by saying nice things or flattering them
notes.zh: "软磨硬泡、甜言蜜语地哄"（画面：小孩缠着爸妈买玩具——"求求你了""你最好了"），游说语境核心义为哄劝、软磨硬泡
notes.ctx: The wheedling has worked——"软磨硬泡起了作用"。区别persuade （讲道理说服）、coax（温柔地哄）：wheedle 是甜言蜜语加死缠烂打。美国政府不能亲自开矿，只能哄企业去海外买矿，一个wheedling 写尽"求着企业下场"的窘态
notes.ex1: He wheedled his parents into buying him a new phone.他软磨硬泡让父母给他买了部新手机。
notes.ex2: The government's wheedling finally persuaded firms to invest abroad.政府的软磨硬泡最终说服了企业到海外投资。

notes.en: in response means as a reaction to something that has happened or been said
notes.zh: "作为回应"，关联语境核心义为作为回应、针锋相对地
notes.ctx: 作者用in response 点明中国是"回应"美国的——你先动154 亿，我回敬一笔更大的。是针尖对麦芒，不是各玩各的
notes.ex1: In response, Chinese giants spent even more abroad. 作为回应，中国巨头在海外砸了更多钱。
notes.ex2: The company cut prices in response to falling demand. 面对需求下滑，公司降低了价格。

notes.en: splurge means to spend a lot of money on something, often in a way that seems careless or showy
notes.zh: "挥霍、大手大脚花钱"（发工资那天一高兴splurge on a new phone），消费语境核心义为豪掷、挥霍
notes.ctx: 作者不用invest（理性的投资），偏用splurge（冲动的挥霍），暗指中国这笔钱砸得"壕气"——"你出154 亿？行，那我出300 亿"。well over $30bn 是美国的近两倍
notes.ex1: Chinese firms splurged well over thirty billion dollars abroad. 中国企业豪掷了远超300 亿美元的海外投资。
notes.ex2: She splurged on a new car after her promotion. 升职后她奢侈地买了辆新车。

paragraphs.en_html: So far the biggest <mark class="voc">beneficiary</mark> has been the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). Most Western investors abandoned the vast, <mark class="voc">conflict-torn</mark>, <mark class="voc">landlocked</mark> central African country when prices of tin, diamonds and other of its abundant resources <mark class="voc">collapsed</mark>. The Chinese have <mark class="voc">pledged</mark> $1bn to expand a copper mine and propose to build a much bigger one that could <mark class="voc">churn out</mark> up to 500,000 tonnes per year.
paragraphs.zh: 截至目前，最大的赢家当属刚果民主共和国。曾几何时，锡、钻石等丰饶物产的价格一泻千里，大多数西方投资者纷纷撤离这个幅员辽阔、战乱不休、深居内陆的中非国家。而中国则承诺斥资10亿美元扩建一座铜矿，并计划再建一座年产可高达50万吨的更大矿山。

notes.en: beneficiary means a person or group who receives an advantage or money from something
notes.zh: "得到好处的人"（词根bene- 拉丁语"好"；同源benefit 好处、benevolent 仁慈的），利益语境核心义为受益者、得利者
notes.ctx: 保险单上的"受益人"就是beneficiary。作者先说the biggest beneficiary 再甩名字，是在吊胃口——最肥的肉被谁叼走了
notes.ex1: So far the biggest beneficiary has been the Democratic Republic of Congo. 到目前为止，最大的受益者是刚果民主共和国。
notes.ex2: She is named as the sole beneficiary of the insurance policy.她被列为这份保单的唯一受益人。

notes.en: conflict-torn means badly affected by war or fighting
notes.zh: "被战乱撕碎的"（conflict 冲突+ torn 是tear"撕扯"的过去分词），战争语境核心义为战乱不断的、满目疮痍的
notes.ctx: 名词+过去分词构成复合形容词——torn 的画面是一块布被两头一扯撕成两半。同类构词war-torn、drought-stricken、smoke-filled，见到"名词-分词"译作"被……的"
notes.ex1: The vast, conflict-torn country has rich mineral deposits. 这个辽阔而战乱不断的国家拥有丰富的矿藏。
notes.ex2: Aid agencies struggle to work in the war-torn region. 援助机构难以在这个饱受战乱的地区开展工作。

notes.en: landlocked means surrounded by land, with no coast or seaport
notes.zh: "被陆地锁死的"（land 陆地+ locked 锁住的），地理语境核心义为内陆的、没有出海口的
notes.ctx: 画面是被一圈国家围在中间、像锁在柜子里。刚果金不靠海，矿挖出来还得借道别人的港口，运输成本与政治风险全上来了。三个形容词vast、conflict-torn、 landlocked 串出"又大、又乱、又不靠海"
notes.ex1: The landlocked country must export its minerals through neighbours. 这个内陆国家必须借道邻国出口矿产。
notes.ex2: Being landlocked raises the cost of everything it trades. 地处内陆抬高了它所有贸易的成本。

notes.en: collapse means to fall down or fail suddenly and completely
notes.zh: "一起塌下来"（col- 一起+ lapse 滑、倒——楼轰的一下塌成废墟），经济语境核心义为崩塌、暴跌、崩溃
notes.ctx: 作者不用fall（下跌）、decline（下滑），用collapse——"雪崩式"暴跌。锡价、钻石价一崩，利润没了，西方资本"弃船而逃"，才有中国抄底
notes.ex1: Prices of tin and diamonds collapsed, driving investors away. 锡和钻石价格暴跌，赶走了投资者。
notes.ex2: The company collapsed under a mountain of debt. 这家公司被堆积如山的债务压垮了。

notes.en: pledge means to make a formal or serious promise to do something
notes.zh: "郑重承诺、立誓"（比promise 口头答应分量重，白纸黑字、当众表态），承诺语境核心义为郑重承诺、保证
notes.ctx: The Chinese have pledged $1bn——中国不是随口说给点钱，是郑重承诺砸10 亿美元。注意用的是expand（扩建），不是新建，是"加码、做大"
notes.ex1: The Chinese have pledged one billion dollars to expand a copper mine. 中国承诺拿出10 亿美元扩建一座铜矿。
notes.ex2: The government pledged to halve emissions by 2030. 政府承诺到2030 年将排放量减半。

notes.en: churn out means to produce large quantities of something quickly, often with little care
notes.zh: "像搅黄油一样源源产出"（churn 搅乳器——搅啊搅，黄油不停出），量产语境核心义为大批量快速产出
notes.ctx: 比produce（生产）多一层"量+速度"。churn out up to 500,000 tonnes per year——年产最高50 万吨，是"巨无霸"级大矿。作者还在敲全文那个"快"字
notes.ex1: The new mine could churn out up to 500,000 tonnes a year. 这座新矿年产最高可达50 万吨。
notes.ex2: The factory churns out thousands of phones every day. 这家工厂每天量产数千部手机。

paragraphs.en_html: Now America is back, too. A government-financed fund is <mark class="voc">in talks to</mark> buy 40% of one of the last remaining Western-owned operating mines, a copper <mark class="voc">concern</mark> run by Glencore, a Swiss-based company. Private firms have followed. The DRC is so <mark class="voc">indigent</mark> that the cash is already transforming its economy. In 2025 foreign mining investment was <mark class="voc">equivalent to</mark> roughly 8% of its GDP.
paragraphs.zh: 如今，美国也杀了回来。一个政府出资的基金正在洽谈，欲购得西方人硕果仅存的在营矿山之一——一座由瑞士巨头嘉能可运营的铜矿——的四成股权。私人资本亦随之跟进。刚果金赤贫如斯，这笔钱已然在改写它的经济；2025年，外资矿业投资竟相当于其GDP的约8%。

notes.en: in talks to means having formal discussions with someone in order to reach an agreement
notes.zh: "正在洽谈"（talks 会谈），商务语境核心义为正在谈判、商谈
notes.ctx: 高频短语。in talks with someone 跟某人洽谈；in talks to do something 谈判准备做某事。A fund is in talks to buy 40%——一个基金正在谈判要买四成股权
notes.ex1: A government-financed fund is in talks to buy 40% of the mine. 一个政府出资的基金正在洽谈收购该矿40% 的股权。
notes.ex2: The two companies are in talks over a possible merger. 两家公司正就可能的合并进行谈判。

notes.en: concern, in business, means a company or business organisation
notes.zh: "操心的事→ 生意"（最早是"跟你有关系、你操心的事"，慢慢指代"公司"），商务语境核心义为公司、企业
notes.ctx: 熟词僻义——不是"担心、关心"，是"公司"。a copper concern 铜业公司；a going concern 持续经营的企业。外刊财经新闻高频
notes.ex1: The mine is a copper concern run by a Swiss-based company. 这座矿是一家由总部在瑞士的公司运营的铜矿企业。
notes.ex2: The firm remains a going concern despite the losses. 尽管有亏损，这家企业仍持续经营。

notes.en: indigent means extremely poor, so poor that one cannot afford basic things
notes.zh: "赤贫的、活不下去的"，贫困语境核心义为极度贫困的、赤贫的
notes.ctx: 比poor（一般穷）、impoverished（贫困）都重——是穷到连最基本东西都买不起。作者不用poor 用indigent，是要强调刚果金不是"穷"，是"赤贫"，所以才说那点钱就能改它的命
notes.ex1: The DRC is so indigent that the cash is already transforming its economy. 刚果金赤贫到如此地步，这些钱已在改变它的经济。
notes.ex2: The clinic offers free care to indigent patients. 这家诊所为赤贫病人提供免费诊疗。

notes.en: equivalent to means equal in value, amount or meaning to something else
notes.zh: "相当于、等同于"（equal 相等+ -valent 价值），比较语境核心义为相当于、等同于
notes.ctx: be equivalent to 高频短语。investment was equivalent to roughly 8% of GDP——投资相当于GDP 的约8%。roughly 是"大约"
notes.ex1: Foreign mining investment was equivalent to roughly 8% of its GDP. 外资矿业投资相当于其GDP 的大约8%。
notes.ex2: The tax cut is equivalent to about 500 dollars per household. 这次减税相当于每户约500 美元。

paragraphs.en_html: Two other big winners are Brazil and Kazakhstan. But they are nevertheless benefiting <mark class="voc">mightily</mark> from American and Chinese interest. America’s approach has been the more focused. In Brazil it has <mark class="voc">set about</mark> building a <mark class="voc">rare-earth empire</mark>. In September USA Rare Earth <mark class="voc">took over</mark> Serra Verde, the only producer of four of the <mark class="voc">scarcest</mark> such minerals outside Asia. A further package pulled together by the Department of War and a loan from the DFC will push American investment to nearly $5bn.
paragraphs.zh: 另外两个大赢家，是巴西与哈萨克斯坦。尽管如此，它们仍从中美两国的浓厚兴趣中获益巨大。美国的手法更为聚焦——在巴西，它已着手营建一座"稀土帝国"。9月，美国稀土公司接管了SerraVerde，这是亚洲以外唯一能生产那四种最稀缺稀土矿物的矿山。由"战争部"牵头拼凑的另一套方案，加上DFC的一笔贷款，将把美国的投资推高至近50亿美元。

notes.en: mightily means to a very great extent, or with great force
notes.zh: "用力地、威力十足地"（might 力量+ -ly），程度语境核心义为极大地、强力地
notes.ctx: benefiting mightily——不是小赚，是"赚疯了"。语感递进：benefit（受益） ＜benefit greatly（受益很大）＜benefit mightily（受益巨大到形容不过来）
notes.ex1: Brazil and Kazakhstan are benefiting mightily from the rivalry. 巴西和哈萨克斯坦正从这场对抗中获益巨大。
notes.ex2: The team fought mightily to stay in the game. 这支队伍拼尽全力留在比赛中。

notes.en: set about (doing something) means to start doing something, especially something that needs a lot of time or effort
notes.zh: "着手开干"（撸起袖子开始干一件大事），行动语境核心义为着手、开始（做大事）
notes.ctx: set about building a rare-earth empire——着手去建一个稀土帝国。自带"正式上马、认真开干"的气势，不是随便试试
notes.ex1: In Brazil, America has set about building a rare-earth empire. 在巴西，美国已着手打造一个稀土帝国。
notes.ex2: She set about reorganising the whole department. 她着手重组整个部门。

notes.en: a rare-earth empire is a complete, self-controlled supply chain for rare-earth minerals
notes.zh: "稀土帝国"（rare earth 稀土+ empire 帝国——一大片地盘我说了算、建立自己的秩序），战略语境核心义为稀土帝国、全链条自主的稀土供应体系
notes.ctx: 帝国不是一个公司、一笔买卖，是"从挖矿到提纯到造磁体全链条由我掌控"。美国不是来"买点矿"，是来建一套"脱离中国"的稀土体系
notes.ex1: America is trying to build a rare-earth empire outside China. 美国正试图在中国之外建立一个稀土帝国。
notes.ex2: He built a business empire from a single shop. 他从一家小店起家建起了商业帝国。

notes.en: take over means to gain control of something, especially a company
notes.zh: "接过来、接管"（新老板上台把旧管理层全换了），控制语境核心义为接管、收购、拿下控制权
notes.ctx: 与buy 不同——buy 买的是所有权，take over 接过来的是"控制权"，强调控制。USA Rare Earth took over Serra Verde 美国稀土公司接管了这座矿
notes.ex1: USA Rare Earth took over Serra Verde in September. 美国稀土公司于9 月接管了Serra Verde。
notes.ex2: The larger firm took over its smaller rival last year. 那家大公司去年接管了它较小的竞争对手。

notes.en: scarce means not easy to find or get; scarce goods are in short supply
notes.zh: "稀缺的、难搞到的"（scarcest 是最高级"最稀缺的"），资源语境核心义为稀缺的
notes.ctx: four of the scarcest such minerals 那四种最稀缺的稀土——钕、镨、镝、铽，是造永磁体（导弹、电动车、风电的"方向盘"）的命根子材料。注意scarce 不读 /skeɪs/，是/skers/
notes.ex1: Serra Verde is the only producer of four of the scarcest minerals outside Asia. Serra Verde 是亚洲之外唯一能生产那四种最稀缺矿物的矿山。
notes.ex2: Water is becoming scarce in many parts of the world. 在世界许多地方，水正变得越来越稀缺。

paragraphs.en_html: In Kazakhstan America is <mark class="voc">eyeing</mark> <mark class="voc">tungsten</mark>, which is vital to high-tech arms-manufacturing. In November 2025 Kaz Resources, a firm <mark class="voc">backed by</mark> the administration and by investors including Eric Trump and Donald Trump junior, is <mark class="voc">stumping up</mark> $1bn to develop deposits at Kairakty and Northern Katpar. A further $1.6bn could come via the DFC and EXIM. Last year Mr Trump’s officials spoke about <mark class="voc">recruiting</mark> countries to America’s camp while pressing them to <mark class="voc">spurn</mark> Chinese <mark class="voc">advances</mark>. Most, they said, would have to <mark class="voc">pick a side</mark>. The experience of the DRC, Brazil and Kazakhstan shows that this is not how things have <mark class="voc">played out</mark> so far.
paragraphs.zh: 在哈萨克斯坦，美国盯上了钨——它对高科技武器的制造至关重要。2025年11月，KazResources——这家由美国政府、以及埃里克·特朗普与小唐纳德·特朗普等投资者支持的公司——掏出10亿美元开发凯拉克特与北卡特帕尔的矿藏，另有16亿美元或经DFC与EXIM注入。去年，特朗普的官员曾扬言要拉各国入美国阵营，同时施压它们唾弃中国的示好，并称大多数国家终须选边站队。然而，刚果金、巴西与哈萨克斯坦的经历表明，事态至今并非如此。

notes.en: eye (as a verb) means to look at someone or something carefully, especially because you want it
notes.zh: "用眼睛盯"（eye 眼睛→ 动词化"盯、虎视眈眈"），关注语境核心义为盯着、垂涎地打量
notes.ctx: America is eyeing tungsten——美国"盯上"了钨。画面是一只鹰盘旋半空、眼睛死死锁定猎物，带着"志在必得"的贪婪劲。进行时eyeing 表"正在盯"
notes.ex1: America is eyeing tungsten for its military value. 美国正盯上钨，看中它的军事价值。
notes.ex2: Several firms are eyeing the struggling company as a takeover target. 几家公司正把这家陷入困境的企业当作收购目标盯着。

notes.en: tungsten is a very hard, grey metal with the highest melting point of all metals
notes.zh: "钨"（元素符号W，源自其拉丁名Wolfram），材料语境核心义为钨
notes.ctx: 两大绝活——熔点3422℃ 为金属之最、极硬，故有"工业牙齿""战争金属之王"之称。穿甲弹弹芯、导弹飞机发动机都靠它。中国掌控全球约八成钨供应，美国自 2015 年起无在营商业钨矿
notes.ex1: Tungsten is vital to high-tech arms manufacturing. 钨对高科技武器制造至关重要。
notes.ex2: The country controls most of the world's tungsten supply. 该国掌控着全球大部分的钨供应。

notes.en: backed by means supported financially or otherwise by a person or organisation
notes.zh: "背后站着……"（back 后背→ 谁在背后撑腰、掏钱），支持语境核心义为由……支持、出资
notes.ctx: a firm backed by the administration——一家由美国政府撑腰的公司。看谁backed by 谁，就知道这笔生意的靠山是谁
notes.ex1: The firm is backed by the administration and by private investors. 这家公司由政府和私人投资者支持。
notes.ex2: The start-up is backed by several large venture funds. 这家初创公司由几家大型风投基金支持。

notes.en: stump up means to pay an amount of money, often unwillingly (informal British English)
notes.zh: "咬牙掏出钱来"（stump 树桩——像从树桩底下刨钱一样掏），口语语境核心义为（不情愿地）掏钱、出钱
notes.ctx: 英式口语。与pay（中性付钱）不同，stump up 带着"肉疼、咬牙"的味道。 is stumping up $1bn——咬着牙掏出10 亿美元
notes.ex1: The firm is stumping up one billion dollars to develop the deposits. 这家公司掏出10 亿美元开发这些矿藏。
notes.ex2: He finally stumped up for the repairs he had promised. 他最终不情愿地掏钱做了他承诺的维修。

notes.en: recruit means to persuade people to join or support something
notes.zh: "招募、征兵"（recruit soldiers 招新兵），拉拢语境核心义为招募、拉拢
notes.ex1: Officials spoke about recruiting countries to America's camp.官员谈到要招募各国加入美国阵营。
notes.ex2: The party is recruiting new members before the election.该党在选举前招募新成员。

notes.en: spurn means to reject someone or something in a proud or angry way
notes.zh: "轻蔑地一脚踢开"（把别人递来的东西啪地打掉），拒绝语境核心义为唾弃、轻蔑地拒绝
notes.ctx: 比refuse（中性说"不"）、reject（正式否决）都狠——是"我不光不要，还看不起你"。pressing them to spurn Chinese advances 逼它们把中国伸来的橄榄枝一脚踢开
notes.ex1: Washington pressed them to spurn Chinese advances.华盛顿施压它们拒绝中国的示好。
notes.ex2: She spurned his offer of help and walked away.她轻蔑地拒绝了他的帮助，转身离开。

notes.en: advances means attempts to start a friendly or romantic relationship, or to win favour
notes.zh: "主动靠近、示好"（make advances 套近乎），关系语境核心义为示好、拉拢、主动接近
notes.ctx: 熟词僻义——不是"前进"，是"示好、套近乎"。Chinese advances 中国的示好、拉拢。注意常用复数，且常与make 连用make advances
notes.ex1: The two powers are both making advances to the same countries. 两个大国都在向同样那几个国家示好。
notes.ex2: He rejected the advances of his rivals and stood firm. 他拒绝了对手的示好，立场坚定。

notes.en: pick a side means to choose which of two opposing groups or views you support
notes.zh: "选边站"（pick 挑+ side 边、阵营），立场语境核心义为选边站、站队
notes.ctx: 美国官员的原话大意——"大多数国家必须二选一，要么跟美国要么跟中国"。这是冷战"谁不跟我们谁就是敌人"逻辑的翻版
notes.ex1: Most countries, they said, would have to pick a side. 他们说，大多数国家都得选边站。
notes.ex2: She refused to pick a side in the argument. 她拒绝在这场争论中站队。

notes.en: play out means to develop or end in a particular way
notes.zh: "（一出戏）演完"（剧情怎么走、怎么收场），发展语境核心义为发展、演变、收场
notes.ctx: how things have played out——事情怎么演变。this is not how things have played out 事情根本没照美国设想的演。转折句：美国要各国选边，结果三国全在"脚踏两条船"
notes.ex1: This is not how things have played out so far. 事情至今并未如此发展。
notes.ex2: Let's wait and see how the situation plays out. 我们等着看事态如何演变。

paragraphs.en_html: American and Chinese <mark class="voc">mineral-hunters</mark> are <mark class="voc">piling into</mark> the same <mark class="voc">handful</mark> of countries because only so many have lots of <mark class="voc">half-finished</mark>, old or <mark class="voc">dormant</mark> mines that can be completed or <mark class="voc">revived</mark> quickly and cheaply. Now America is becoming impatient—and so behaving more like the Chinese.
paragraphs.zh: 中美两国的矿产猎手，正一窝蜂地挤进同样那寥寥几个国家——因为只有那么几个地方，坐拥大量烂尾、老旧或休眠的矿山，能够又快又省地完工或重启。如今，美国愈发不耐烦，行事也越来越像中国了。

notes.en: a mineral-hunter is a person or company that searches for minerals to acquire
notes.zh: "矿产猎手"（mineral 矿+ hunter 猎手——扛着枪、眼睛冒光、满山找猎物），商业语境核心义为矿产猎手、四处搜寻矿藏的人
notes.ctx: 作者不说"矿业公司"，偏说"猎手"——那种"四处搜寻、发现就扑上去"的劲一下出来了。American and Chinese mineral-hunters 两个猎手抢同一批猎物
notes.ex1: American and Chinese mineral-hunters are piling into the same countries. 中美两国的矿产猎手正一窝蜂挤进同样那几个国家。
notes.ex2: Bargain hunters rushed to buy shares after the crash. 暴跌之后，抄底者蜂拥买入股票。

notes.en: pile into means to get into a place or activity in large numbers, in a disorderly way
notes.zh: "一窝蜂挤进"（pile 堆——公交车来了，一群人呼啦全往上挤），涌入语境核心义为蜂拥而入、一窝蜂挤进
notes.ctx: piling into the same handful of countries——两边挤的是同一扇门。注意same（一样的）：美国去的中国也去
notes.ex1: Investors are piling into the same small group of countries. 投资者正蜂拥涌入同样那一小群国家。
notes.ex2: Fans piled into the stadium hours before the match. 球迷们在开赛前数小时就蜂拥入场。

notes.en: a handful of means a small number of people or things
notes.zh: "一把"（手抓一把米，就那么点），数量语境核心义为少数几个、寥寥几个
notes.ex1: Only a handful of countries have such ready mines. 只有少数几个国家有这样的现成矿山。
notes.ex2: A handful of investors made most of the profits. 少数几个投资者赚走了大部分利润。

notes.en: half-finished means only partly completed
notes.zh: "建了一半的"（half 一半+ finished 完工的），状态语境核心义为烂尾的、未完工的
notes.ctx: 画面是烂尾楼——盖到一半、钢筋外露、停工多年。half-finished mines 烂尾矿：有人投了钱、建了一半，资金断了或跑了就撂那儿。是"别人已经花过大钱"的矿
notes.ex1: The country has lots of half-finished, old or dormant mines.这个国家有大量烂尾的、老旧的、休眠的矿山。
notes.ex2: The half-finished tower has stood empty for years.那座建了一半的塔已经空置多年。

notes.en: dormant means not active for the time being, but able to become active again
notes.zh: "休眠的、蛰伏的"（dormant volcano 休眠火山——现在不喷但没死，哪天就醒），状态语境核心义为休眠的、蛰伏的
notes.ctx: 三个形容词里最有味道的一个——表面是"停的"，其实是"睡着的、随时能醒"。dormant mine 休眠矿：曾开过、后来停了、矿还在、随时能重启
notes.ex1: A dormant mine can be revived quickly and cheaply.一座休眠矿能又快又便宜地重启。
notes.ex2: The volcano has been dormant for a century.这座火山已休眠了一个世纪。

notes.en: revive means to bring something back into use or make it active again
notes.zh: "复活、苏醒"（re- 再+ vive 活——同源vivid 生动的、survive 幸存），恢复语境核心义为复活、重启、使复苏
notes.ex1: Old mines can be revived at a fraction of the cost of new ones.老矿可以以远低于新矿的成本重启。
notes.ex2: The government hopes to revive the struggling economy.政府希望重振低迷的经济。

paragraphs.en_html: In the short run, <mark class="voc">smash-and-grab</mark> may benefit the superpower rivals, too. Yet the strategy has its limits. It relies on others to <mark class="voc">prospect</mark> for and develop existing deposits, even as prospectors and developers grow more cautious. Despite forecasts of surging demand for copper, which may <mark class="voc">outstrip</mark> supply by 8% within ten years, the world’s biggest producer of <mark class="voc">the red metal</mark>, Chile, has <mark class="voc">cut back</mark> output, largely owing to underinvestment in <mark class="voc">decaying</mark> assets.
paragraphs.zh: 短期内，"砸橱窗抢劫式"的抢矿或能让两个超级大国对手也分得一杯羹。但这套策略自有其局限：它仰赖他人去勘探、开发现成的矿藏，而勘探者与开发者却正日趋谨慎。尽管预测铜需求将激增、十年内或超供给8%，全球最大的"红金属"生产国智利反而减产，主因是对日渐老化的矿山投资严重不足。

notes.en: smash-and-grab is a robbery in which a window is broken and goods are snatched quickly; figuratively, quick grabbing without thought for the future
notes.zh: "砸橱窗抢劫"（smash 砸+ grab 抢——砸碎玻璃、抓了就跑），比喻语境核心义为抢现成、不管长远的掠夺
notes.ex1: Smash-and-grab may benefit the rivals in the short run.短期内，这种抢现成的做法可能让对手受益。
notes.ex2: Thieves carried out a smash-and-grab raid on the jewellery shop.窃贼对珠宝店实施了一次砸窗抢劫。

notes.en: prospect (as a verb) means to search for minerals or other valuable substances
notes.zh: “勘探、找矿”（pro- 向前+ spect 看——淘金者东张西望到处找金矿），矿业语境核心义为勘探、找矿
notes.ex1: The strategy relies on others to prospect for and develop deposits. 这套策略靠别人去勘探和开发现成的矿藏。
notes.ex2: Thousands once came to prospect for gold in these hills. 曾几何时，成千上万的人来这片山区淘金。

notes.en: outstrip means to become larger, more important or better than something else
notes.zh: "把……甩在后面"（out- 超出+ strip 跑——赛跑时把别人甩下一大截），比较语境核心义为超过、把……甩在后头
notes.ex1: Demand for copper may outstrip supply by 8% within ten years.十年内，铜需求可能超过供给8%。
notes.ex2: Wage growth has outstripped inflation for the first time in years.工资增长多年来首次超过通胀。

notes.en: the red metal is a nickname for copper, which has a reddish-brown colour
notes.zh: "红金属"（铜是唯一天生带红棕色的常见金属），矿业语境核心义为铜
notes.ex1: Chile is the world's biggest producer of the red metal.智利是全球最大的红金属（铜）生产国。
notes.ex2: The price of the red metal hit a record high this year.今年铜价创下历史新高。

notes.en: cut back means to reduce the amount of something
notes.zh: "往回切、缩减"（cut 切+ back 回），减产语境核心义为削减、缩减、减产
notes.ctx: cut back output 减产。全球在闹"铜荒"、铜价飞天，最大的产铜国智利反而减产——这是本段最扎心的反常
notes.ex1: Chile has cut back output despite record copper prices.尽管铜价创纪录，智利反而减产了。
notes.ex2: The company cut back on travel to save money.公司削减差旅以节省开支。

notes.en: decaying means gradually getting worse, falling apart or rotting
notes.zh: "正在腐烂、衰败的"（decay 腐烂——木头被雨淋、被虫蛀一天天烂下去），状态语境核心义为老化的、衰败的
notes.ex1: The mines are decaying assets that nobody wants to fund.这些矿山是没人愿意投资的衰败资产。
notes.ex2: The city's decaying infrastructure needs urgent repair.这座城市日益老化的基础设施急需修缮。

paragraphs.en_html: Higher prices should <mark class="voc">in theory</mark> attract investment in new projects. But these can take a decade or more to <mark class="voc">pinpoint</mark> and develop. In the meantime, all the <mark class="voc">meddling</mark> by the governments of America and China is confusing the <mark class="voc">price signals</mark> miners rely on to decide whether an <mark class="voc">untapped</mark> deposit is <mark class="voc">worth the hassle</mark>. The result is more investment <mark class="voc">paralysis</mark>—but, for the lucky few places with ready deposits, it’s <mark class="voc">payday</mark>. ■
paragraphs.zh: 理论上，高价本该引来对新项目的投资。但新矿往往要十年甚至更久方能定位与开发。而与此同时，中美两国政府的种种插手，正搅乱矿企赖以判断"一处未开发矿藏是否值得大费周章"的价格信号。其结果是更多的投资瘫痪——然而，对那些坐拥现成矿藏的少数幸运之地而言，这却是它们的发薪日。■

notes.en: in theory means according to what should be true, though it may not be so in practice
notes.zh: "理论上"（theory 理论），让步语境核心义为理论上、按道理说
notes.ex1: Higher prices should in theory attract new investment. 理论上，更高的价格应该会吸引新投资。
notes.ex2: In theory it works, but in practice it rarely does. 理论上行得通，实践中却很少行得通。

notes.en: pinpoint means to find or describe something exactly
notes.zh: "用大头针钉住那个点"（pin 大头针+ point 点——在地图上把矿的位置一针钉住），精确定位语境核心义为精确定位、准确找到
notes.ex1: New projects can take a decade or more to pinpoint and develop. 新项目可能要花十年甚至更久才能定位并开发。
notes.ex2: Engineers pinpointed the cause of the failure within hours. 工程师们在数小时内就准确定位了故障原因。

notes.en: meddle means to interfere in something that is not your business, in a way that annoys people
notes.zh: "多管闲事、瞎掺和"（贬义——别人好好做事，你凑过去指手画脚添乱），干涉语境核心义为插手、干涉、添乱
notes.ex1: All the meddling by the two governments is confusing the price signals.两国政府的种种插手正在搅乱价格信号。
notes.ex2: He warned outsiders not to meddle in the country's affairs.他警告外部势力不要干涉该国内政。

notes.en: a price signal is the information that a market price gives to buyers and sellers about supply and demand
notes.zh: “价格信号”（signal 信号、红绿灯），经济语境核心义为价格信号、价格这个 “红绿灯”
notes.ex1: Miners rely on price signals to decide whether to invest. 矿企依赖价格信号来决定是否投资。
notes.ex2: Government subsidies can distort the price signals investors need. 政府补贴会扭曲投资者所需的价格信号。

notes.en: untapped means not yet used or developed, especially resources or potential
notes.zh: "龙头还没拧开的"（tap 水龙头——一口井龙头还没开、水还在地里），资源语境核心义为未开采的、未开发的
notes.ex1: They must decide whether an untapped deposit is worth the hassle. 他们必须判断一处未开发的矿藏值不值得费这个劲。
notes.ex2: The region has vast untapped potential for clean energy. 该地区在清洁能源方面有巨大的未开发潜力。

notes.en: worth the hassle means worth the trouble or effort involved
notes.zh: "值得费这个劲"（hassle 麻烦事、费劲的事），权衡语境核心义为值得费这个劲、值得折腾
notes.ex1: Miners must decide if a new deposit is worth the hassle. 矿企必须判断新矿藏是否值得费这个劲。
notes.ex2: For a small gain, it is simply not worth the hassle. 就为那么点收益，实在不值得折腾。

notes.en: paralysis means a total inability to move or act
notes.zh: “瘫痪、麻痹”（动词paralyze——脑子清醒但身体动不了），停滞语境核心义为瘫痪、停滞
notes.ex1: The result is more investment paralysis in the mining sector.结果是矿业领域的投资瘫痪加剧。
notes.ex2: The committee was stuck in paralysis, unable to reach a decision.委员会陷入瘫痪，无法作出决定。

notes.en: payday is the day on which a person receives their wages or salary
notes.zh: "发薪日"（pay 发工资+ day 日子——打工人最盼的那天），隐喻语境核心义为发薪日、数钱的好日子
notes.ctx: 全文的冷幽默收官——整个行业在"瘫痪"、在煎熬，但少数几个攥着现成矿的国家，照样像打工人一样准时"领工资"。作者用一个payday 加句号收尾，讽刺"大国忙前忙后、小国天天数钱"
notes.ex1: For the lucky few places with ready deposits, it's payday.对少数坐拥现成矿的幸运之地来说，这是发薪日。
notes.ex2: Friday is payday for most of the workforce.对大多数上班族来说，周五是发薪日。

proper.name: rare earth
proper.def:
简要介绍：17 种金属元素的总称（钪、钇加镧系15 种），其实一点都不"稀"——最丰富的铈在地壳里的储量跟铜差不多。名字是个历史误会：1787 年瑞典军官在伊特比村捡到一块黑石头，1794 年芬兰化学家加多林从中分离出"钇土"，因当年习惯把不溶于水的固体氧化物叫"土"、又以为它稀有，故得名"稀土"。"稀"的不是矿，是"把17 个孪生兄弟一个个分开"的分离提纯技术——这一环中国占全球约九成，中国"稀土之父"徐光宪上世纪70 年代的"串级萃取"理论把纯度提到99.99%，让中国从资源大国变成分离霸主。
本文中的意思：全文的命门词。它串起"关键矿产为什么关键"和"中国为什么能卡脖子"——你有矿没用，会不会炼才是关键。

proper.name: cobalt
proper.def:
简要介绍：元素符号Co，银蓝色金属。独门绝技是能让电池存得住电、扛得住高低温——手机、电动车电池靠它，故称"电池的心脏"。全球挖出的钴六成以上最终进入电池厂。刚果金一国产量占全球约七成、储量近一半。
本文中的意思：第一个赢家刚果金的"王牌"。也是全文最扎心的一层——刚果金部分钴来自无安全措施的手工矿，甚至童工，国际媒体称之为"电池的血钻"，你手机里那点钴可能是一个孩子用手挖出来的。

proper.name: World Bank
proper.def:
简要介绍：专门向发展中国家提供资金与贷款的国际机构。它的钱往哪儿砸，通常意味着"哪儿要起风了"。
本文中的意思：10 月16 日宣布把一支关键矿产基金扩至五倍、达200亿美元，帮各国分这波暴涨需求。五年前这类融资才约36 亿美元，翻五倍还多——全世界真金白银往矿里砸。

proper.name: Democratic Republic of Congo / DRC
proper.def:
简要介绍：中非国家，国土约234 万平方公里（非洲第二大），人口一亿多，是联合国认定的"世界最不发达国家"之一，人均GDP 约700 多美元。地底下富得流油（钴、铜），地面上穷得叮当响。注意与"刚果布"（刚果共和国）区分——带"金"字的才是矿产大国。
本文中的意思：全文第一个也是最大的赢家。西方资本在2015-16 年大宗商品崩盘后"弃船而逃"，中国反手抄底（砸10 亿美元扩建铜矿、再造年产50 万吨的巨无霸），美国随后也杀回来。2025 年外资矿业投资相当于其GDP 的约8%——钱一进去，这个赤贫国家的经济整个被"脱胎换骨"。

proper.name: Glencore
proper.def:
简要介绍：总部在瑞士的矿业与大宗商品贸易巨头，全球最大钴生产商之一，在刚果金经营二十多年。旗下Mutanda（穆坦达）是全球最大钴矿之一，最盛时曾供全球约五分之一的钴；另有Kamoto（卡莫托）铜钴大矿。
本文中的意思：美国"杀回来"的落点——政府牵头的基金要买下它在刚果金两座矿山40%的股权，因为这是西方人手里"硕果仅存"的在营矿之一。

proper.name: DFC
proper.def:
简要介绍：U.S. International Development Finance Corporation，美国政府的官方金融机构，专门出资支持美国在海外的战略投资，是"美国政府掏钱抢矿"的主要工具之一。
本文中的意思：在巴西、哈萨克斯坦两处都出现——给稀土矿批贷款、帮钨矿融资，是那套"政府砸钱开路、私企跟上"打法里的钱袋子。

proper.name: EXIM
proper.def:
简要介绍：Export-Import Bank of the United States，美国政府系的金融机构，专门给"美国企业做海外生意"提供贷款与担保。
本文中的意思：与DFC 并列，是哈萨克斯坦钨矿那笔16 亿美元融资的来源之一。

proper.name: Orion
proper.def:
简要介绍：美国一家顶级私募牵头发起、获DFC 支持的关键矿产投资联盟，专门收购海外关键矿产资产。
本文中的意思：美国重返刚果金的主力——通过这个联盟，以约90 亿美元的盘子买嘉能可在刚果金两座矿山40% 的股权，卡住钴的命脉、对冲中国已占七成多的矿山份额。

proper.name: Serra Verde / USA Rare Earth
proper.def:
简要介绍：Serra Verde 是巴西一家稀土矿商，矿山位于巴西中部戈亚斯州的Pela Ema（佩拉埃玛），2024 年初才开始商业生产，却是亚洲之外唯一能规模化生产钕、镨、镝、铽四种磁性稀土的矿山。USA Rare Earth 是美国专门搞稀土的公司，2025 年9 月出手接管了它。
本文中的意思：美国"稀土帝国"的关键一子——巴西稀土储量全球第二（约2100 万吨），产量却不到全球1%（因为缺"分离"技术）。美国拿下这座"亚洲之外唯一"的矿，再叠加DFC 贷款与"战争部"的锁定包购，总投资直逼50 亿美元。

proper.name: Kaz Resources / Kairakty & Northern Katpar
proper.def:
简要介绍：Kaz Resources 是一家去哈萨克斯坦开发钨矿的公司，背后有美国政府背书，以及埃里克·特朗普、小唐纳德·特朗普等投资者。Kairakty（凯拉克特）与NorthernKatpar（北卡特帕尔）是哈萨克斯坦中部两处大型钨矿，属全球最大的未开发钨矿资源之一。
本文中的意思：美国抢钨的抓手。中国掌控全球约八成钨供应、美国自2015 年起无在营商业钨矿——为了挣脱这第二只"锁喉的手"，美国连总统的儿子都下了场。

proper.name: Eric Trump / Donald Trump Jr.
proper.def:
简要介绍：美国总统特朗普的两个儿子。大儿子因与父亲同名，称"小唐纳德"（DonaldTrump Jr.），二儿子为埃里克（Eric Trump）。
本文中的意思：彩蛋级细节——据报道二人通过一家空壳公司入股建筑公司，后者与矿业公司合并为Kaz Resources，而Kaz Resources 又拿到美国政府上十亿美元的融资去挖钨。本文仅陈述事实，不作评论。

proper.name: Chile
proper.def:
简要介绍：全球最大的产铜国，一个国家产了全球约四分之一的铜，堪称"铜界的沙特"。其铜矿多为几十年前的老矿，品位逐年下降。
本文中的意思：全文最讽刺的反常——全球闹"铜荒"、铜价飞天，智利反而减产（2025 年产量同比降约2%），主因是老矿越挖越贫、而所有人都忙着"抢现成"，没人肯掏钱救那些正在衰败的老矿。

proper.name: resource curse
proper.def:
简要介绍：经济学著名现象——自然资源越丰富的穷国，往往越容易穷、越容易乱。典型如委内瑞拉（石油储量全球前列却经济崩盘）、尼日利亚（非洲第一大产油国，老百姓反而最穷）。钱来得太容易，人就懒得干别的，还容易为抢钱内斗。
本文中的意思：开头for better or worse（婚礼誓词）埋的伏笔——资源可能是"祝福"，也可能是"诅咒"。有矿，不一定就是好事。

proper.name: supercycle
proper.def:
简要介绍：大宗商品价格的超长上涨期。历史上有过数轮：19 世纪末美国崛起、二战后欧洲日本重建、1970 年代石油危机、2000 年代中国崛起——每一轮背后都站着一个"巨人在崛起"。2000 年代那轮：铁矿石13→190 美元/吨（13 倍）、铜1800→8900（近4倍）、石油25→147（近6 倍）。
本文中的意思：作者说世界"可能正在进入又一个超级周期"，推手是中美抢关键矿产。这个another 暗示历史又走到熟悉的节点——新一轮巨人崛起。

proper.name: rare-earth magnets / 四种磁性稀土
proper.def:
简要介绍：钕、镨、镝、铽四种稀土是造"永磁体"（永远带磁的磁铁）的核心材料。永磁体用在电动车电机、风力发电机转子，以及导弹与战斗机上控制方向的小电机里——磁体一失效，导弹就失控。故称这四种稀土是"命根子"级的战略物资。
本文中的意思：解释美国为什么非拿下巴西Serra Verde 不可——它是中国之外唯一能稳定供这四种稀土的矿。

proper.name: 2025 稀土出口管制事件
proper.def:
简要介绍：2025 年4 月4 日，中国对钐、钆、铽、镝、镥、钪、钇七种中重稀土实施出口管制（这些是造芯片、武器离不了的）。一个月后的5 月12 日，中美在日内瓦达成声明，美国同意把对华关税从145% 降到30%。
本文中的意思：第三段那段"加关税→限稀土→被迫收手"因果链的实锤。一张稀土牌打出去，关税战直接熄火——这就是美国为什么拼了命要"挣脱锁喉"。
